acrobatics.title: Acrobatics
acrobatics.whatItMeans: Acrobatics covers balance, tumbling, and movement that requires body control.
acrobatics.exampleInPlay: A character might use Acrobatics to keep their footing on a slick roof or slip free from a tight squeeze.
acrobatics.whyItMatters: This skill helps characters move with control when the environment is trying to make movement difficult.

animal-handling.title: Animal Handling
animal-handling.whatItMeans: Animal Handling covers calming, guiding, and understanding animals.
animal-handling.exampleInPlay: A character might use Animal Handling to calm a panicked horse or keep a pack animal from bolting.
animal-handling.whyItMatters: This skill matters when animals are part of the challenge or part of the solution.

arcana.title: Arcana
arcana.whatItMeans: Arcana covers magical theory, spells, and strange supernatural knowledge.
arcana.exampleInPlay: A character might use Arcana to identify a glowing rune or recognize the school of magic behind a spell effect.
arcana.whyItMatters: Arcana is the classic skill for characters who study magic or investigate magical phenomena.

athletics.title: Athletics
athletics.whatItMeans: Athletics covers climbing, swimming, jumping, grappling, and other physical exertion.
athletics.exampleInPlay: A character might use Athletics to haul themselves up a cliff, wrestle an enemy, or swim against a strong current.
athletics.whyItMatters: Athletics is the main skill for doing things with muscle and stamina.

deception.title: Deception
deception.whatItMeans: Deception covers lying, bluffing, disguise of intent, and falsehoods told convincingly.
deception.exampleInPlay: A character might use Deception to pretend they belong somewhere or conceal a bad decision with a confident story.
deception.whyItMatters: Deception is useful for characters who need to mislead people without immediately raising suspicion.

history.title: History
history.whatItMeans: History covers the past, old empires, legends, wars, rulers, and cultural memory.
history.exampleInPlay: A character might use History to recognize a royal crest, remember the name of an old battle, or identify a ruin from its architecture.
history.whyItMatters: History helps characters understand the world by knowing what came before.

insight.title: Insight
insight.whatItMeans: Insight covers reading motives, emotional cues, and hidden intent.
insight.exampleInPlay: A character might use Insight to tell whether a merchant is nervous, hiding something, or telling the truth poorly.
insight.whyItMatters: Insight helps characters understand people beneath the words they are saying.

intimidation.title: Intimidation
intimidation.whatItMeans: Intimidation covers threats, menace, forceful presence, and frightening others into hesitation.
whatItAffects: Using presence to scare or dominate
intimidation.exampleInPlay: A character might use Intimidation to make a guard think twice before standing in the way.
intimidation.whyItMatters: Intimidation works when a character wants people to back off without needing a long argument.

investigation.title: Investigation
investigation.whatItMeans: Investigation covers careful searching, clue gathering, and analysis of details.
investigation.exampleInPlay: A character might use Investigation to inspect a room for hidden compartments or connect clues from a crime scene.
investigation.whyItMatters: Investigation is about thinking carefully and looking closely instead of just noticing things at a glance.

medicine.title: Medicine
medicine.whatItMeans: Medicine covers treating injuries, recognizing wounds, and understanding basic physical condition.
medicine.exampleInPlay: A character might use Medicine to tell whether someone is dying, poisoned, or suffering from a specific injury.
medicine.whyItMatters: Medicine is useful when someone is hurt and you want to understand the problem before acting.

nature.title: Nature
nature.whatItMeans: Nature covers plants, animals, weather, terrain, and the natural world.
nature.exampleInPlay: A character might use Nature to identify a dangerous mushroom, recognize a storm pattern, or understand what lives in a swamp.
nature.whyItMatters: Nature helps characters understand the wild world and survive in it.

perception.title: Perception
perception.whatItMeans: Perception covers noticing hidden details, sounds, movement, and danger.
perception.exampleInPlay: A character might use Perception to notice a concealed trap, hear footsteps behind a wall, or spot someone hiding in the shadows.
perception.whyItMatters: Perception is one of the most commonly useful skills in the game because it helps characters avoid surprises.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to notice danger early

performance.title: Performance
performance.whatItMeans: Performance covers entertaining, performing, speaking dramatically, and presenting yourself well.
performance.exampleInPlay: A character might use Performance to put on a convincing show, play a song, or deliver a speech with flair.
performance.whyItMatters: Performance matters when a character is trying to impress, entertain, or move an audience.

persuasion.title: Persuasion
persuasion.whatItMeans: Persuasion covers convincing others, negotiating, and making a strong argument.
persuasion.exampleInPlay: A character might use Persuasion to talk down a guard, bargain with a merchant, or win support from a noble.
persuasion.whyItMatters: Persuasion is the skill for getting people to agree with you by sounding reasonable and credible.

religion.title: Religion
religion.whatItMeans: Religion covers gods, rites, cults, holy symbols, and sacred traditions.
religion.exampleInPlay: A character might use Religion to identify a deity's symbol, interpret a shrine, or understand an old rite.
religion.whyItMatters: Religion helps characters recognize the beliefs and sacred practices that shape the world.

sleight-of-hand.title: Sleight of Hand
sleight-of-hand.whatItMeans: Sleight of Hand covers subtle hand work, quick fingers, and small-scale trickery.
sleight-of-hand.exampleInPlay: A character might use Sleight of Hand to slip a key from someone's belt or hide a coin in their palm without being noticed.
sleight-of-hand.whyItMatters: This skill is for characters who work quietly with their hands instead of making a scene.

stealth.title: Stealth
stealth.whatItMeans: Stealth covers moving quietly, hiding, and avoiding notice.
stealth.exampleInPlay: A character might use Stealth to move through a guarded hallway without being seen or heard.
stealth.whyItMatters: Stealth is what lets characters stay unnoticed when that is exactly the point.

survival.title: Survival
survival.whatItMeans: Survival covers finding your way, tracking creatures, foraging, and enduring the wilderness.
survival.exampleInPlay: A character might use Survival to follow tracks through the woods, find safe shelter, or judge which direction leads home.
survival.whyItMatters: Survival helps characters keep moving and stay alive when the environment itself is part of the challenge.
